title: Deep roots (Avot 3:17)
hookLine: wisdom greater than deeds is a tree with many branches and few roots
tomorrow: two math geniuses with no bread. who noticed?

cards: A tree in a parking-lot strip can look full and green, and one storm tips it over with roots the size of a fist. Elazar ben Azariah knew that tree.
Someone whose wisdom is greater than their deeds, he says, is like a tree with many branches and few roots: the wind comes and turns it over.
Someone whose deeds are greater than their wisdom is a tree with few branches and many roots: all the winds in the world can blow, and it won't move.

teach.b: He backs each tree with Jeremiah: one like a bush in the desert, one like a tree planted by water, sending its roots out toward the stream. Roots are the deeds nobody sees.
It's Chanina ben Dosa's deeds first from earlier in this chapter, told as a tree. And it's a good lens for the week. Everyone, cheerfully: the hello as a root.
Silence fences wisdom: quiet that guards the soil.
Beloved, and told so: the love that reaches someone. Foreseen, yet free: the step that's yours.
The hand writes: every deed on the page. No flour, no Torah: bread and learning, holding each other up. Each one is something to do, not only something to know.
And notice his balance. He isn't against wisdom; the steady tree still has branches. He's asking which grows faster, and which you'd rather have when the wind comes.

how: Jews read Avot 3:17's two trees with Jeremiah 17, and the saying is often taught as a reason to let practice keep pace with study.

o: deeds that outgrow your wisdom and hold you up
a strong faith that never has any doubts
a family tree that goes back many generations

games.q: this week's lines — tap the pairs.

s: in Elazar's parable, the tree with many branches stands firm
many branches and few roots: the wind turns it over.
Elazar backs his two trees with verses from Jeremiah
a bush in the desert, and a tree planted by water.

games.q: your new roommate is cold to you all week. which of this week's lines applies first?
o: everyone, cheerfully: receive them with joy, and go first.
silence fences wisdom: say nothing to them at all.
foreseen, yet free: it was meant to be, so wait it out.
games.why: Ishmael's line asks you to receive every person with joy; silence is a fence for your words, not a wall against people.

practice: Sit still and choose one sound around you, the hum of a fridge, traffic, your own breath, and stay with it. When your mind starts growing branches, ideas about the sound, come back down to the sound itself.

wordCard.voice: Deep roots. Elazar's steady tree: deeds that outgrow wisdom hold it in the ground.

orig.note: Hebrew: roots, like the many roots of Elazar's steady tree.

carryVoice: The line: deep roots, so let the wind blow. A whole week of Avot, rooted and still standing.

sources.ref: Mishnah Avot 3:9 (Chanina ben Dosa: deeds exceeding wisdom)
